note: Facts checked Nov 12, 2026. Statuses change: missions that end are removed.

craft.name: ISS
craft.about: The largest structure humans have built in space, about 400 km up, with people living aboard without a break since November 2000. It circles Earth about every 92 minutes.
timeline: Space Shuttle's last visit; assembly largely complete

craft.name: Tiangong
craft.about: China's space station, about 390 km up, crewed by taikonauts in rotations of about six months. Its three modules were joined in 2022.
timeline: Third module, Mengtian, joined: the T shape complete

craft.name: Hubble
craft.about: The Hubble Space Telescope, about 510 km up, has photographed the universe in visible, ultraviolet and near-infrared light since 1990. Astronauts serviced it five times.
timeline: First servicing mission corrects its mirror

craft.name: Chandra
craft.about: NASA's X-ray observatory, on a long, stretched orbit reaching about a third of the way to the Moon. It sees the hottest places in the universe: exploded stars, black holes and galaxy clusters.

craft.name: XMM-Newton
craft.about: ESA's X-ray observatory, on a stretched two-day orbit up to about 115,000 km from Earth. Its three telescopes collect more X-rays than any before it.

craft.name: Fermi
craft.about: NASA's gamma-ray telescope, about 530 km up, which maps the whole sky every three hours in the highest-energy light.

craft.name: NuSTAR
craft.vehicle: Pegasus XL, from an aircraft over the Pacific
craft.about: A NASA telescope that focuses high-energy X-rays, using a 10-metre mast unfolded in space, to study black holes and the remains of exploded stars.

craft.name: TESS
craft.about: NASA's planet hunter, on an orbit that swings out close to the Moon's distance every 13.7 days. It watches nearby stars for the tiny dips in light made by planets passing in front of them.

craft.name: CHEOPS
craft.about: ESA's small telescope that measures the sizes of planets already found around nearby stars, about 700 km up.

craft.name: IXPE
craft.about: Measures the polarisation of X-rays from black holes and neutron stars, about 600 km up; built by NASA with the Italian Space Agency.

craft.name: XRISM
craft.about: A Japanese-led X-ray telescope, about 550 km up, that splits X-rays into very fine colours to measure the gas between galaxies.

craft.name: Einstein Probe
craft.about: A Chinese Academy of Sciences X-ray telescope, with ESA and Germany's Max Planck Institute as partners, that watches wide areas of sky for sudden X-ray flashes.

craft.name: SVOM
craft.about: A French–Chinese satellite that catches gamma-ray bursts, the brightest explosions in the universe, and points its telescopes at them within minutes.

craft.name: SPHEREx
craft.about: Maps the whole sky in 102 infrared colours, every six months, to study how the universe began and where the ingredients of life are found.

craft.name: SMILE
craft.full: Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer
craft.about: An ESA–Chinese Academy of Sciences mission that images how the solar wind strikes Earth's magnetic field, from a stretched orbit reaching far above the North Pole.

craft.name: James Webb
craft.about: The largest space telescope, seeing in infrared light, in a loop around the point L2, about 1.5 million km from Earth on the side away from the Sun.

craft.name: Euclid
craft.about: ESA's telescope mapping billions of galaxies across a third of the sky, to study dark matter and dark energy, near L2.

craft.name: Roman
craft.about: NASA's wide-field infrared telescope, with a view a hundred times wider than Hubble's at the same sharpness, working near L2.

craft.name: SOHO
craft.about: Has watched the Sun without a break from the point L1, 1.5 million km towards the Sun, since 1996, and has found more than 5,000 comets in its pictures.

craft.name: ACE
craft.about: Samples the solar wind at L1 about an hour before it reaches Earth, giving warning of space weather.

craft.name: Wind
craft.about: One of NASA's oldest working spacecraft, measuring the solar wind near L1 since 2004.

craft.name: Aditya-L1
craft.about: India's first solar observatory, in a loop around L1 since January 2024, watching the Sun's outer layers and the solar wind.

craft.name: IMAP
craft.about: Studies the solar wind and the edge of the heliosphere, the bubble the Sun blows around the solar system, from L1.

craft.name: Parker Solar Probe
craft.about: Flies through the Sun's outer atmosphere, closer to the Sun than any spacecraft before it: 6.1 million km from its surface at its closest, at about 690,000 km/h.
timeline: First spacecraft to fly through the Sun's corona
First closest pass: 6.1 million km from the surface

craft.name: Solar Orbiter
craft.about: ESA's mission taking the closest pictures of the Sun and, as its orbit tilts, the first views of the Sun's poles.

craft.name: STEREO-A
craft.about: Orbits the Sun slightly inside Earth's orbit, so it sees the Sun from a different angle and drifts slowly ahead of Earth.

craft.name: Voyager 1
craft.about: The farthest human-made object, more than 25 billion km away, in interstellar space since 2012. It flew past Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980.

craft.name: Voyager 2
craft.about: The only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune, in interstellar space since 2018.

craft.name: New Horizons
craft.about: Flew past Pluto in 2015 and the small, far world Arrokoth on 1 January 2019; now crossing the Kuiper belt.

craft.name: Juno
craft.about: Orbiting Jupiter since 2016 on long loops over its poles, studying its clouds, deep interior and magnetic field, and flying past its moons.

craft.name: Europa Clipper
craft.about: On its way to Jupiter's icy moon Europa, to find out whether the ocean under its ice could support life. It arrives in 2030.

craft.name: JUICE
craft.about: ESA's mission to Jupiter and three of its large moons, Ganymede, Callisto and Europa, to learn whether their buried oceans could support life. It uses flybys of the Moon, Earth and Venus to gain speed on the way.

craft.name: Lucy
craft.about: On a twelve-year tour of the Trojan asteroids that share Jupiter's orbit, the first mission to visit them.
timeline: Flies past the asteroid Dinkinesh and finds its moon

craft.name: Psyche
craft.about: On its way to the metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche, pushed by electric (ion) thrusters; it arrives in 2029.

craft.name: OSIRIS-APEX
craft.about: As OSIRIS-REx it brought samples of the asteroid Bennu to Earth in 2023; renamed, it is on its way to the asteroid Apophis, which passes close to Earth in April 2029.

craft.name: Hera
craft.about: ESA's mission to the asteroid pair Didymos and Dimorphos, to measure what NASA's DART probe did when it struck Dimorphos in 2022: a test of moving an asteroid.
timeline: Mars flyby, past its moon Deimos
Arrives at Didymos, at the end of 2026

craft.name: BepiColombo
craft.about: Two orbiters, ESA's and JAXA's, travelling together to Mercury; they separate once in orbit around it.

craft.name: Hayabusa2
craft.about: Brought samples of the asteroid Ryugu to Earth in 2020, then set off on an extended mission; it meets the small, fast-spinning asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031.

craft.name: Tianwen-2
craft.about: China's mission to collect samples from the small near-Earth asteroid Kamoʻoalewa, a possible piece of the Moon, and bring them to Earth, then go on to a comet.
timeline: Sample capsule due back at Earth

craft.name: ESCAPADE
craft.full: Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers
craft.about: Two small identical spacecraft, Blue and Gold, built to study how the solar wind strips Mars's atmosphere, from two orbits at once. They reach Mars in 2027.
timeline: Earth flyby, then the burns towards Mars

craft.name: Mars Express
craft.about: ESA's first mission to another planet, orbiting Mars since December 2003; its radar found signs of buried water ice.

craft.name: Mars Odyssey
craft.about: The longest-working spacecraft at Mars, in orbit since October 2001; it mapped ice under the surface and relays messages from the rovers.

craft.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
craft.about: Orbiting Mars since 2006; its HiRISE camera can see objects the size of a kitchen table, and it relays data from the rovers.

craft.name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
craft.about: Sniffs the thin Martian air for gases that could come from geology or life, and relays data from NASA's rovers.

craft.name: Hope
craft.about: The United Arab Emirates' first planetary mission, on a high orbit that shows the weather on the whole of Mars at once.

craft.name: Tianwen-1
craft.about: China's first Mars mission: its orbiter, still working, carried the Zhurong rover, which landed in May 2021.

craft.name: Curiosity
craft.about: A car-sized rover in Gale crater since August 2012, climbing Mount Sharp and reading its layers of rock like pages of Mars's history.

craft.name: Perseverance
craft.about: A rover in Jezero crater since February 2021, collecting rock samples in sealed tubes from an ancient river delta.

craft.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
craft.about: Mapping the Moon since 2009 in great detail, including the Apollo landing sites and the cold, dark craters near the poles.

craft.name: Chandrayaan-2
craft.about: India's lunar orbiter, mapping the Moon since 2019; it also relayed for Chandrayaan-3's lander, which touched down near the south pole in 2023.

craft.name: Danuri
craft.about: Korea's first lunar mission, in orbit around the Moon since December 2022, carrying a NASA camera that looks into permanently shadowed craters.

craft.name: Terra
craft.about: NASA's first big Earth-watching satellite, measuring land, ocean, clouds and air since 2000.

craft.name: Aqua
craft.about: Follows Earth's water: evaporation, clouds, rain, ice and snow.

craft.name: Aura
craft.about: Measures the ozone layer and air quality.

craft.name: Landsat 8
craft.about: Part of the longest-running record of Earth's land from space, begun in 1972.

craft.name: Landsat 9
craft.about: Works with Landsat 8 so that every place on land is pictured every eight days.

craft.name: Sentinel-1C
craft.about: A radar satellite of the EU's Copernicus programme: it sees the ground through cloud and darkness.

craft.name: Sentinel-2B
craft.about: Takes colour pictures of land and coasts for Copernicus, in 13 colours from blue to infrared.

craft.name: Sentinel-2C
craft.about: Takes colour pictures of land and coasts for Copernicus; it went up on the last flight of the original Vega rocket.

craft.name: Sentinel-3A
craft.about: Measures the oceans' height, temperature and colour for Copernicus.

craft.name: Sentinel-3B
craft.about: Works with Sentinel-3A on the oceans' height, temperature and colour.

craft.name: Sentinel-5P
craft.about: Maps the gases polluting the air every day.

craft.name: Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich
craft.about: Measures sea level to within a few centimetres, continuing a record begun in 1992.

craft.name: CryoSat-2
craft.about: Measures the thickness of sea ice and the ice sheets.

craft.name: SMOS
craft.about: Measures the moisture in soil and the saltiness of the sea.

craft.name: EarthCARE
craft.about: Studies how clouds and tiny particles in the air warm or cool the planet, with a radar and a laser.

craft.name: Biomass
craft.about: The first space radar long enough in wavelength to see through forest canopies and weigh the world's forests.

craft.name: Suomi NPP
craft.about: A weather and climate satellite; its night-time camera shows city lights and fires.

craft.name: NOAA-20
craft.about: One of the polar-orbiting satellites behind every weather forecast.

craft.name: NOAA-21
craft.about: The newest of the polar-orbiting weather satellites.

craft.name: GOES-18
craft.about: The GOES-West weather satellite, 35,786 km up over the Pacific, where it keeps pace with Earth's turning.

craft.name: GOES-19
craft.about: The GOES-East weather satellite, 35,786 km up over the Americas; it also carries a coronagraph that watches the Sun.

craft.name: Himawari-9
craft.about: Japan's weather satellite, 35,786 km up over the western Pacific.

craft.name: Meteosat-12
craft.about: Europe's newest-generation weather satellite (MTG-I1), 35,786 km up over Africa; it also detects lightning.

craft.name: SWOT
craft.about: Surveys the height of nearly all water on Earth: oceans, lakes and rivers.

craft.name: PACE
craft.about: Sees the colour of the ocean in fine detail to track plankton, and the haze and clouds above it.

craft.name: ICESat-2
craft.about: Measures the height of ice, sea, land and trees with a laser, 10,000 pulses a second.

craft.name: GRACE-FO
craft.full: Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Follow-On
craft.about: Two satellites, one following the other about 220 km behind, that weigh moving water and ice by tiny changes in the distance between them.

craft.name: GPM
craft.about: The core of a fleet measuring rain and snow around the world every 30 minutes.

craft.name: SMAP
craft.about: Maps the water in the top few centimetres of soil every few days.

craft.name: NISAR
craft.about: A radar built by NASA and ISRO together that measures movements of land and ice of a centimetre or less.

craft.name: WSF-M1
craft.about: The first of the US Space Force's new weather satellites, measuring winds over the ocean with a microwave imager; its orbit is published.
